Team — kicking off this week’s fleet / pipeline sync. Short summary and asks below; please read the attached pipeline_snapshot_Q2.xlsx and reserve_cost_model_v1.xlsx before EOD so we can lock decisions for Friday’s commit call.

Quick context: Q2 bookings have pushed forward several mid-size deals (Acme, Polaris) with aggressive latency SLAs. We need to decide reserve vs burst mix for committed capacity in May-July to avoid last-minute scrambling and preserve predictable unit economics.

Agenda / asks (30 min read + 15 min call):
- Review current pipeline delta vs. last week (tab: forecast_delta).
- Finance: confirm acceptable unit economics on 6/12-month reserve tiers — see reserve_cost_model_v1.xlsx.
- Infra: feasibility on 2 additional reserved pools (r4-common, r4-highmem) + 25% burst headroom.
- Sales: prioritize which 3 deals get dedicated priority slots if we need to trim.

Key decision points I want by 4pm PT Thursday:
1) Commit to number of reserved slots for May–Jul (per pool).
2) Approve 90-day burst credit tranche for high-touch closes.
3) Agree on deal priority (Acme vs Polaris vs AtlasAI).

Attachments: pipeline_snapshot_Q2.xlsx (xlsx), reserve_cost_model_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — Steph

Thanks Steph — rapid notes from infra: we reviewed the snapshot and stress-tested the May–Jul window against current pool allocations. TL;DR: we can carve the two pools but there are tradeoffs.

Observations: 
- Current baseline utilization across fleets: r3-general 72%, r3-highmem 66%, burst consumption up 18% W/W.
- If we add r4-common (32 GPUs) + r4-highmem (16 GPUs) as reserved pools for May, we’ll need to reassign ~24 GPUs from flexible burst supply unless we accept a temporary reduction in burst availability.

Options (feasible) — pick one: 
A) Reserve-only conservative: Add both pools as reserved (48 GPUs) and reduce burst pool by 24 GPUs. This preserves latency SLOs but increases cost per token by ~8% for Q2 (see reserve_cost_model_v1.xlsx).
B) Hybrid (recommended): Reserve r4-common 24 GPUs + r4-highmem 8 GPUs; keep burst flat and rely on spot-like transient capacity for 16 GPUs. This gives a small latency uplift for heavy tails but keeps unit-cost impact to ~3–4%.
C) Minimal reserve: Only r4-common 12 GPUs (pilot) — lowest near-term spend, highest risk for preclose jitter.

Infra asks: 
- Finance signoff on hybrid scenario (B) so we can provision on Monday 4/19.
- Sales: confirm the top two priority deals you want pinned to reserved slots (we’ll mark them as priority routing in the control plane).

Attachment: I exported the utilization snapshots into the shared drive (see link).

— Ben

Quick update from Sales side: priority mapping below based on closes expected in the next 6 weeks. Numbers are conservative but capture committed/most-likely per HubSpot.

Priority 1 — Acme Corp (KEVIN)
- ARR impact: $1.2M annualized if pilot converts.
- Preferred: dedicated low-latency pool; must support consistent <80ms p95 for inference.
- Ask: pin 12 reserved GPUs (r4-common) and 8 burst credits for pilot month. Kevin, we’ll confirm exact start date in the next email.

Priority 2 — Polaris Health (procurement@polarishealth.com)
- ARR: $480k estimated.
- Need: high-memory variants for larger models, prefer r4-highmem 8 GPUs reserved; can tolerate 100–120ms p95.

Priority 3 — AtlasAI (ops@atlasai.co)
- ARR: $320k. Flexible on start; can take spot/burst for initial 30 days.

If Infra supports Ben’s hybrid (B), Acme gets pinned reservations first, Polaris second, AtlasAI uses burst. That maps cleanly to our priority list and minimizes customer risk while keeping qtr economics reasonable.

- Burst credit tranche: 120 hours equivalent of high-priority burst (can be consumed across pools).
